title: Opinion
description: A STORED opinion: the model's response after the system has attached its provenance. Two variants selected by `role`. NOTE the boundary - `model_id`, `prompt_version` and `prompt_sha256` are required here but the prompts forbid the model from emitting them (it cannot know its own prompt hash); the runner attaches them before validating. G2 therefore validates the object that gets stored, not the fragment that came off the wire. G3 separately checks that every index in relies_on_facts is within range of the case's agreed_facts array - a bound the schema cannot express because it depends on the case.

prompt_sha256.description: Hash of the prompt file at call time. Lets an opinion be traced to the exact text that produced it, and makes an un-bumped version header detectable.

relies_on_facts.description: Zero-based indices into the case's agreed_facts. May be empty only for an opinion that expressly rests on the absence of a fact, and then `no_facts_reason` is required.

case_for_seat.description: The strongest case for this advocate's SEAT, argued in good faith from the agreed record - regardless of what the advocate personally concludes. Added turn 005. The baseline showed three runs in five where every advocate reached the same position, so the judges received no opposing argument at all: 'the seat does not fix the position' was collapsing into 'nobody argues the unpopular side'. This field guarantees both cases are put. It does NOT constrain `position`, which remains free.

position.description: The advocate's own conclusion, which MAY contradict both its seat and its own `case_for_seat`. No gate may require agreement between `position` and `seat` - the instructor's simulation rule fixes the procedural role only. Divergence is recorded and reported, never blocked.

argument.description: Why this advocate personally lands where `position` says - which may be adopting `case_for_seat`, or departing from it and saying why. In character. Must not be a copy of `case_for_seat`; G2 checks.

concedes.description: What this advocate accepts against its own seat. Optional, and its presence is a health signal: four advocates that concede nothing are probably one advocate.

ruling.description: The permitted rulings, from the case's scope.decides. No third value. An opinion that cannot reach one of these is a failed call, not an abstention.

grounds.description: The load-bearing reasons, each stated so that another judge could disagree with it specifically.

reasoning.description: The opinion in the voice of the method.

responds_to.description: Direct answers to advocate arguments. At least two, matching the instruction in the judge prompts. A judge that answers no one has not judged the case that was argued. The further requirement - that at least one answered advocate sits in the seat ruled against - depends on the case and is checked by G2b in code, not here. `answer` was capped at 600 characters until turn 004, when the cap discarded an entire judge opinion over one long sentence; raised to 1200, which still forbids an essay per answer.

disclaimer.description: Carried as data, not as page decoration, so it cannot be lost in a redesign. Checked by G6.

not.$comment: scope.imposes_sentence is false and scope.combines_opinions is false. There is deliberately nowhere in this shape to put a sentence, a combined result, or one judge's assessment of another. Checked structurally by G6 rather than by reading prose.
